subject.title: exec auto-reviewer re-bills a fresh model completion for every byte-identical repeated exec

question: May OpenClaw reuse model-backed exec reviewer decisions for byte-identical requests, and what exact cache lifetime and key are acceptable for the exec approval boundary?
rationale: The redundant completion path is clear, but caching an exec approval reviewer result changes when later requests bypass fresh model review, so maintainer intent is needed before automation changes that boundary.

options.title: Approve full-input per-run memo
options.body: Cache parsed reviewer decisions only inside the shared reviewer instance, keyed by the full reviewed input or prompt, and never persist or convert them to durable approval.

options.title: Cache allow-once only
options.body: Memoize only low-risk allow-once results and keep ask, error, and timeout results uncached for a narrower approval-boundary change.

options.title: Keep fresh review semantics
options.body: Accept repeated reviewer completion cost to preserve one-request-one-review behavior until stronger live billing or security evidence changes the tradeoff.

recommendation.title: Approve full-input per-run memo
recommendation.body: Cache parsed reviewer decisions only inside the shared reviewer instance, keyed by the full reviewed input or prompt, and never persist or convert them to durable approval.
